facts.content: Patient presents with acute dizziness or vertigo described as room spinning, with unsteady gait, ear buzzing, and nausea.
facts.source_text: CC: acute dizziness/vertigo, room spinning, unsteady gait, ear buzzing, nausea

facts.content: Dizziness began approximately 2 hours ago.
Patient had a similar but shorter episode of dizziness one month ago lasting 5 to 10 minutes.
facts.source_text: similar shorter episode 1 month ago (5–10 min)

facts.content: Patient has had constant dizziness since onset.
Patient reports no vomiting.
Patient reports no fever.
Patient reports no recent viral illness.
Patient reports no ear pain or discharge.
Hearing is otherwise intact aside from buzzing.
Patient reports no limb weakness or focal neurological symptoms.
facts.source_text: No limb weakness or focal neurological symptoms reported

facts.content: Patient has a history of premature ovarian failure.
Patient is taking hormone replacement therapy.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient has acute vertigo with suspected labyrinthitis clinically diagnosed.
Patient has nausea associated with vertigo.
Semitol 1 tablet three times daily is prescribed for 10 days to be sent to Lloyd Pharmacy.
facts.source_text: Prescribe semitol 1 tab TID — send 10 days to Lloyd Pharmacy

facts.content: Patient is given symptomatic advice to use paracetamol for fever if needed.
facts.source_text: Symptomatic advice: paracetamol for fever if needed

facts.content: Patient is advised to take semitol with or without food according to tolerance.
facts.source_text: take semitol with or without food per patient tolerance

facts.content: A face-to-face review is to be arranged with a doctor for ear examination, blood pressure check, and gait and neurological examination.
facts.source_text: Arrange face-to-face review with doctor for ear examination, BP check, gait/neuro exam

facts.content: Patient is advised to go to A&E if new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, persistent or violent vomiting, or deterioration occurs.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: go to A&E if new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, persistent/emesis/violent vomiting or deterioration

facts.content: Patient is to call support to book an in-person appointment.
facts.source_text: Patient to call support to book in-person appointment
